To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a radioligand initially developed to identify growth hormone-releasing hormone receptors in rat anterior pituitary was found to specifically identify a high affinity subclass of VIP receptors.

the (125I-HIS1, D-AlA2, NLEU27)-GRF peptide, initially developed as possible GRF radioligand, binds to a high-affinity VIP receptor in rat liver membranes and that this binding is specific, reversible, saturable, and sensitive to GTP and divalent cations.

(1) a growth hormone-releas- ing factor analog was found to bind specifically to high-affinity VIP receptors in liver membranes, (2) the binding was saturable, and (3) the dissociation was accelerated in the presence of guanine nucleotides.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization and quantification of a subclass of VIP receptor in rat liver membranes which is specifically identified by a GRF analog.

the development of a radioligand that can be used to study the distribution and regulation of high-affinity VIP receptors in mammalian tissues. (125I)-His1, D-ala2, Nle27)-GRF (1-29) is a potential candidate for this purpose.
the identification of a high-affinity VIP receptor in rat liver membranes, which is labelled by a GRF analog.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
(125I- His1, D-AlA2, Nle27)-GRF (1-29)NH2 specifically labels a high-affinity vassactive intestinal peptide receptor subclass in rat liver membranes.
the (125I-HIS1, D-ALA2, NLEU27)-GRF (1-29) NH2 is not a specific radioligand of the GRF receptor in the anterior pitutary.
(125I-Tyr1, D-Alal, Nleu26)-VIP is a specific ligand of VIP receptors in liver membranes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
(125I- His1, D-Al2, Nleul7)-GRF( 1-29)- NH2 is a useful radioligand to study VIP receptors.

(125I-DPhe6, D-Phe12)-VIP is a suitable radioligand to identify the high-affinity VIP receptor subtype in rat liver, whereas (125I-Hist, D-Ala 2, Nle27)-GRF is a suitable radiotracer to identify the high- affinity VIP receptor in rat brain membranes.
(125I-Tyr1, D-Phe2)-VIP is a specific and stable radioligand that can be used to characterize high-affinity VIP receptors in a variety of rat tissues.
The main takeaway from our work is that
(125I-D-Ala2)-VIP is an excellent tool to identify VIP receptors in rat brain and that these receptors are present in the same areas as GRF receptors, but are different.
(His1, d-Ala2, Leu27)-GRH (1-29) NH2 is a useful tool to identify a subclass of VIP receptors.
the GRF analogue is a useful tool for identifying and characterising VIP receptors in rat hepatic tissue.
